characters.identity_anchors: Adult male of indeterminate exact age; face capable of shifting from forced calm composure to extreme nervous agitation; eyes alert and listening; no scars or distinctive marks specified; body language of exaggerated caution and later uncontrolled frenzy
characters.source_evidence: True!—nervous—very, very dreadfully nervous I had been and am; disease had sharpened my senses—not destroyed—not dulled them; above all sense of hearing acute; how healthily—how calmly I can tell you the whole story; I was never kinder; I fairly chuckled; I grew furious; I smiled gaily; I was singularly at ease then grew pale; I foamed—I raved—I swore
characters.voice_label: tense intimate first-person male voice, initially controlled and persuasive, rising to frantic shrieking

wardrobe_variants.description: Simple period civilian day clothes suitable for a household resident speaking heartily to the old man each morning
source_facts: every morning when the day broke I went boldly into the chamber and spoke courageously to him calling him by name in a hearty tone
I was never kinder to the old man than during the whole week before I killed him
wardrobe_variants.creative_direction: Muted earth-tone waistcoat shirt and trousers of mid-19th-century lower-middle domestic cut; neat but not wealthy; no blood or disorder; calm open collar

wardrobe_variants.description: Dark close-fitting night or house clothes allowing silent movement; hands free for lantern and door latch
source_facts: about midnight I turned the latch of his door and opened it—oh so gently
I put in a dark lantern all closed
I thrust in my head
I moved it slowly—very very slowly
A watch’s minute hand moves more quickly than did mine
wardrobe_variants.creative_direction: Near-black or deep charcoal soft fabric shirt and trousers; stockinged or soft-soled feet; sleeves that will not snag; face partially shadowed; no jewelry or reflective metal except the lantern

wardrobe_variants.description: Same civilian day clothes now worn with forced lightness of heart while receiving police; later disheveled by pacing and rage
source_facts: I went down to open it with a light heart
I smiled—for what had I to fear
I bade the gentlemen welcome
I was singularly at ease
I felt myself getting pale
I paced the floor to and fro with heavy strides
I foamed—I raved—I swore
I swung the chair
wardrobe_variants.creative_direction: Day clothes slightly rumpled from night labor yet still presentable at first; collar loosened as agitation grows; no visible blood (tub caught all); final state sweat-darkened and disordered

characters.identity_anchors: Elderly male; one pale blue eye with a film over it described as a vulture eye; the rest of the face and person kept in darkness except when the single ray strikes the eye; frail enough to be dragged to the floor and covered by his own heavy bed
characters.source_evidence: I loved the old man; He had never wronged me; He had the eye of a vulture—a pale blue eye with a film over it; Whenever it fell upon me my blood ran cold; the old man who vexed me but his Evil Eye; he lay upon his bed; the old man sprang up in bed; His room was as black as pitch; I could see nothing else of the old man’s face or person; he shrieked once—once only; Yes he was stone stone dead; His eye would trouble me no more
characters.voice_label: aged male voice thin with sleep and terror; single cry of 'Who’s there?' and one shriek

wardrobe_variants.description: Nightshirt or simple sleeping garment in bed under covers; later corpse state after dismemberment (head arms legs separated)
source_facts: he lay upon his bed
the old man sprang up in bed
I dragged him to the floor and pulled the heavy bed over him
I cut off the head and the arms and the legs
deposited all between the scantlings
wardrobe_variants.creative_direction: Plain unbleached or white linen nightshirt; bare or stockinged feet; no spectacles or other eye covering; body remains covered by bed until murder; post-dismemberment only implied by wrapped or bagged forms under floor never lingering on gore

characters.identity_anchors: Three adult males; introduced with perfect suavity; manner calm and official; remain seated chatting pleasantly and smiling even as narrator deteriorates; no individual names or distinguishing features given
characters.source_evidence: there came a knocking at the street door; There entered three men who introduced themselves with perfect suavity as officers of the police; A shriek had been heard by a neighbour; they had been deputed to search the premises; I bade the gentlemen welcome; The officers were satisfied; My manner had convinced them; they sat and while I answered cheerily they chatted of familiar things; still they sat and still chatted; the men chatted pleasantly and smiled; Was it possible they heard not
characters.voice_label: calm measured official male voices; polite conversational tone; no raised alarm until after confession

wardrobe_variants.creative_direction: Dark wool frock coats or early police tunics with simple badges or buttons; tall hats or caps removed indoors; gloves optional; clean and composed appearance throughout; three similar but not identical builds
